title: Netflix Unveils the Official Trailer for 'The Child'
summary: The new film by Mariano Barroso and starring Goya Award winners Belén Cuesta and Karra Elejalde
body_markdown:
Entertainment


12 October 2026


Global


Spain


Link copied to clipboard


###


THE FILM HITS THEATERS ON NOVEMBER 13, BEFORE ITS PREMIERE ON NETFLIX ON NOVEMBER 27


[Watch the trailer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vsXs3Km6UDw)


[Download the poster](https://assetshare.netflixstudios.com/488900b3-2df1-434b-b8df-2bd6f3e8d582)


[Download the new images](https://assetshare.netflixstudios.com/ff0538a9-2707-4a19-b72c-19fa67728c9c)


Netflix has unveiled today the official trailer for


The Child


, the new film by


Mariano Barroso


(


Ecstasy


,


Todas las mujeres


,


La línea invisible


) and starring Goya Award winners


Belén Cuesta


(


The Endless Trench


,


Money Heist


) and


Karra Elejalde


(


Spaish Affair


,


While at War


). The Child will hit cinemas on


13 November


, ahead of its


Netflix release on 27 November


.


Based on the novel by


Fernando Aramburu


, the film weaves a fictional story around a real tragedy, focusing on grief, family ties, and the different ways of coping with loss. “It is only when one is faced with an extreme situation and the need to overcome it, that one discovers one’s true strength. That is what


The Child


is about: the need to find what is indestructible within us,” says Mariano Barroso, the film’s director and screenwriter.


Barroso,


Goya Winner for Best Adapted Screenplay for


Todas las mujeres


alongside


Alejandro Hernández


, produces the film with


Rafael Portela


(Umea Films)- The cast is rounded off by


Pep Ambròs


(


Burning Body


,


The Olive Tree


),


Raquel Ferri


(


God's Crooked Lines


),


Joan Solé


(


See You in Another Life


), and the young actor


Alex Infantes


(


The Crystal Cuckoo


).


SYNOPSIS:


The Child


tells the story of Mariaje (


Belén Cuesta


) and Nicasio (


Karra Elejalde


), the mother and grandfather of one of the children who died in a gas explosion in a town in the Basque Country in October 1980. The tragedy shocked the local community and the whole of Spain, changing their lives forever. On a journey marked by unexpected emotions, Mariaje and Nicasio search for —and find— their own unique way to overcome their loss.


Paola Vallejo


Senior Publicity Manager
